study_identification.title: Towards Longitudinal Characterization of Multiple Sclerosis Atrophy Employing SynthSeg Framework and Normative Modeling

study_characteristics.study_objective: To investigate deviations in subcortical volumes in MS patients using advanced deep learning segmentation models (SynthSeg+ and SynthSeg-WMH) on T1-weighted and FLAIR MRI data, and comparing these volumes to a normative model from a large healthy cohort to enhance the characterization of MS progression.
study_characteristics.study_design_other: Mixed cross-sectional and longitudinal design. Some subjects had data from two time points.

model_origin_detail.answer: The CentileBrain [18] model trained with 37,407 healthy individuals (53.3% females, age range 3-90) from 81 datasets. The CentileBrain employs Multivariate Factorial Polynomial Regression (MFPR) [38] algorithm. See Ge et al. (2024) for details.

response_variable.answer: Subcortical volumes: Thalamus, Caudate, Putamen, Pallidum, Hippocampus, Amygdala, and Accumbens

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The paper uses a pre-trained model (CentileBrain) and does not describe the validation of the normative model itself.

clinical_dataset.answer: A heterogeneous dataset comprising 326 MS patients from five sources: three in-house datasets (Lausanne University Hospital (CHUV), Louvain Neuroinflammation Imaging Lab (NIL), and Imaging Axonal Damage & Repair in Multiple Sclerosis (INsIDER) [20]) and two public datasets (MICCAI-MSSEG2016 challenge [8] and OpenMSLong [30]).

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: The study analyzed the trajectories of the Z-scores against age. No association with clinical variables was performed.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The study demonstrates the feasibility of using normative models and deep learning-based segmentation to identify and quantify brain atrophy in MS patients, showing increasing deviation with age in the thalamus.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study found that DL models can estimate subcortical volumes in MS patients, with results comparable to literature values. The FLAIR sequence was found to be relevant for characterizing certain subcortical structures. The deviation from the normative model (Z-scores) showed an increasing trend with age in the thalamus of MS patients. SynthSeg+ and SynthSeg-WMH showed different performance depending on the region.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study is a pilot study with a limited sample size. The reference values for volume comparison are based on T1w images, which could bias the results. The study did not include lesion load analysis. Manual lesion segmentations were not available for all datasets.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study highlights the potential of integrating DL with normative modeling to refine MS progression characterization. It also suggests that FLAIR sequences can be highly relevant for adequate characterization of certain subcortical structures.

general_notes.general_notes: The study uses two different deep learning segmentation models, SynthSeg+ and SynthSeg-WMH, and compares their performance on T1w and FLAIR images. The study uses a pre-trained normative model called CentileBrain. The study uses ComBat-GAM for site harmonization of the clinical data.
